newsitem.title: USA: Fire hazard leads to upscale clothing recall.
newsitem.headline: Fire hazard leads to upscale clothing recall.

text.p: Sweaters and bathrobes sold by three upscale retailers and sweat shirts sold by discounter Target are being recalled after tests showed they could catch fire easily, a federal agency announced Monday.
The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission said fabrics that fail these flammability tests typically burn more quickly than newspaper.
The agency and Melcon Design LLC of New York jointly agreed to recall four styles of long-haired rayon chenille sweaters sold by Nordstrom and smaller retailers under the brand name "Relais."
The sweaters sold for $80 to $150 in crop crew, fitted cardigan with collar, fitted polo with collar and turtleneck tunic styles. Other styles of "Relais" brand chenille sweaters were not recalled.

Neiman Marcus Group Inc. joined with the CPSC in a recall of 6,500 terrycloth bathrobes for men and women made by Egeria International. The robes sold for $220-$330 in a variety of colours and styles at Neiman Marcus and the company's Bergdorf Goodman department store.
The stores said they were aware of four incidents of the bathrobes igniting when exposed to flame but knew of no injuries.

The CPSC and Target Stores of Minneapolis, owned by Dayton Hudson Corp., recalled 106,000 fleece sweat shirts for men and boys sold under the brand name "Utility." The sweat shirts sold for $18 to $22 and were made of a cotton-polyester blend fabric, often called sherpa, which has a fleecy texture made to resemble an inside-out sweat shirt.
The CPSC and the companies involved in the recalls said the clothes should be returned to the store where purchased for a full refund.
